entries.title: Proverbs 29:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Judgment - By the free and impartial exercise of justice. Gifts - Bribes.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wrath - The wrath of God or of men, who were enraged against it.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Whether - Whether he, the wise man, deal sharply with him, or mildly, there is no rest, no end or fruit of the debate.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Left - Suffered to follow his own will without restraint and chastening.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No vision - No prophecy; no publick preaching of God's word.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A servant - Who is so not only in condition, but also in the temper of his mind, disingenuous, and stubborn. Words - By mere words. Tho' - Though he know thy mind, and his own duty.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hasty - Who is rash and heady in the management of his affairs.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Delicately - Allowing him too much freedom, and familiarity. A son - Will find him at last grow insolent, and forgetful of his servile condition.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bewrayeth it not - Which he is bound to do for the publick good.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A snare - Is an occasion of many sins.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Judgment - The decision of his cause, and the success of all his endeavours.
